description: The relations family fed by live PromQL against lgtm-prometheus, where Tempo's metrics-generator remote-writes the service graph. Two routes: a plain ranged query with an empty Transform tab, which draws every edge but gives them all one id; and an instant table reshaped with organize + rowsToFields, which gives each edge a name an override can address. Both are portable to any Prometheus with Tempo's metrics-generator behind it.

options.content:
# Prometheus → relations charts

Tempo's metrics-generator publishes `traces_service_graph_request_total{client, server}` and remote-writes it into **`lgtm-prometheus`** (`lgtm/config/tempo.yaml`). Those two labels are a real source/target pair, which is what makes this stack useful to this panel family — the same metric a Grafana Cloud or Mimir user already has.

The panel reads endpoints from two carriers, in this order: the `source` / `target` **labels** on a field, then a `-->` in the field **name**. `client` / `server` is neither, so every query below renames the pair with `label_replace`. Two routes follow from that:

### Route A — a ranged query and an empty Transform tab

```promql
sum by (source, target) (
  label_replace(
    label_replace(
      sum by (client, server) (rate(traces_service_graph_request_total{client!="", server!=""}[$__rate_interval])),
      "source", "$1", "client", "(.*)"),
    "target", "$1", "server", "(.*)"))
```

`Format: Time series` returns **one frame per series**, each `[Time, Value]` with the grouping labels on `Value`. Every one of those frames passes the reader's edge test on its own, and the reader collects *all* of them — so nine series draw nine edges with no transformation anywhere. The row dimension survives too, which is why **Calculation** is a real choice here: `Last` is the current rate, `Mean` is the average over the window.

What it does **not** give you is identity: every value field is called `Value`, so all nine marks share one id. `byName: 'Value'` matches all of them at once, and a per-edge unit, colour or data link is unreachable. (On Grafana 13.2+ the plugin pivots this shape into named fields itself, above the panel — this host is 13.1.0, so it does not.)

### Route B — an instant table, `label_join`, `organize`, `rowsToFields`

```promql
label_join(
  label_replace(
    label_replace(
      sum by (client, server) (rate(traces_service_graph_request_total{client!="", server!=""}[$__range])),
      "src", "$1", "client", "(.*)"),
    "dst", "$1", "server", "(.*)"),
  "edge", "-->", "src", "dst")
```

`Format: Table` + `Type: Instant` is one row per series; `rowsToFields` turns each row into a field named by its first **string** column. Two details are load-bearing, and both are visible in the bottom-right panel:

- **`organize` must put `edge` first.** Prometheus sorts label columns alphabetically, so the first string column is `client` — a bare `rowsToFields` would name every mark after its *client* and produce duplicate fields with no endpoints at all.
- **the query names the pair `src` / `dst`, and `organize` renames it** to `source` / `target`. Not the other way round: a query that emits `source` and `target` *columns* is claimed as the legacy row format by the conversion the plugin registers above the panel on 13.2+, which then widens it before this chain runs — and the panel shows **No data** with nothing logged. Renaming inside the Transform tab happens strictly after that pre-pass, so it is safe on every host.

The payoff is a field per edge, named `grafana-->prometheus`, which the `/-->/ ` overrides in the panels below actually address.

panels.title: Route A — service dependency map, no transformations
panels.description:
Nine ranged series, an empty Transform tab, and the whole service graph. Every frame carries `source` / `target` labels on its `Value` field, so each one passes the edge test alone and the reader collects them all.

The legend format is set to `{{source}}-->{{target}}` even though nothing here reads it: on Grafana 13.2+ the plugin's pivot promotes exactly that rendered legend to `field.name`, so writing it now means this panel gains per-edge ids on upgrade with no dashboard change. Today it only labels the tooltip series.

`prometheus → prometheus` is Prometheus scraping itself — a genuine self-loop, which a graph draws and a sankey cannot. `user` is Tempo's virtual node: requests with no client span.

panels.title: Route B — the same graph, with per-edge ids
Edges and node stats — two queries, two filtered chains
panels.description:
Route B for the edges (refId A) plus a second query (refId B) giving each service its **error ratio**, which becomes the node colour. Both chains are scoped with `filter: byRefId` so neither touches the other's frames, and `rowsToFields` stamps its output `rowsToFields-A` / `rowsToFields-B`, so a later `byRefId` cannot recapture an earlier chain's result.

The node query is bounded with `and on (server) …` to the servers the edges actually reach: a node field for a service no edge touches renders as a disconnected dot.

Nodes are percentages against green/orange/red thresholds. The single `byRegexp: /-->/ ` override puts every edge back on `reqps` **and** back on a palette colour — that colour property is required, not cosmetic: an edge left on `thresholds` resolves a threshold colour instead of deferring to the link-colour mode, so a healthy graph would draw all-green edges. The override is addressable at all only because Route B named the edges.

The layout is `force` with **Repulsion**, **Edge length** and **Gravity** set. All three are Advanced-tier options, and an Advanced option that is set while `editorMode` is left at `default` is discarded before it reaches the chart — so this panel's JSON also carries `"editorMode": "advanced"`, as every panel here that sets one does. Left unset, ECharts' own repulsion default of 50 collapses seven nodes into a single blob.

**Why the error ratio is wrapped in `or … * 0`.** `traces_service_graph_request_failed_total` does not exist for a service that has never failed, and a division whose left side has no series returns **nothing** — so `prometheus` and `alloy` got no node field at all, and the reader fell back to deriving them from the edges. A derived node has no field, so it takes a classic-palette colour by position: the panel looked as if the threshold colours were broken, when in fact two thirds of the nodes had no stat. `or <total> * 0` supplies the zero those services deserve, and all six nodes then resolve green/orange/red. `user` stays palette-coloured on purpose — it is Tempo's virtual node, never a `server`, so no query can give it a ratio.

targets.expr:
label_replace(
  (
    (
        sum by (server) (rate(traces_service_graph_request_failed_total[$__range]))
      or
        sum by (server) (rate(traces_service_graph_request_total[$__range])) * 0
    )
    / sum by (server) (rate(traces_service_graph_request_total[$__range]))
  )
  and on (server)
  sum by (server) (
    sum by (client, server) (
      rate(traces_service_graph_request_total{client!="", server!=""}[$__range])
    )
  ),
  "node", "$1", "server", "(.*)"
)

panels.title: Span metrics: service → operation — sankey
panels.description:
A different metric from the same generator: `traces_spanmetrics_calls_total{service, span_name}` — one series per operation per service. Restricted to `span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER"` so each call is counted once, at the server, and bounded with `topk(10, …)` because Grafana alone has hundreds of routes.

Bipartite and therefore a genuine DAG, so nothing is dropped here — compare the Tempo dashboard's sankey, which has to break a cycle. Still Route A in the sense that matters: the endpoints are `source` / `target` labels and the Transform tab is empty.

**Two query settings, both load-bearing.** `Type: Instant`, because `topk(N, …)` in a *ranged* query is evaluated at every step and the result is the **union** of each bucket's top N — about thirty operations over an hour, not ten, with labels overlapping into illegibility. And `Format: Time series`, not Table: an instant *table* is one flat frame whose label columns are columns, so the value field carries no labels and the reader finds no edges at all — the panel goes blank. Instant + Time series is one frame per series with the labels still on `Value`, which is the shape the reader wants. The cost of instant is the row dimension: one row per mark, so every reducer agrees and **Calculation** stops mattering.

**One trap specific to this stack:** `traces_spanmetrics_*` and `traces_service_graph_*` both carry an external label `source="tempo"` (`metrics_generator.registry.external_labels` in `lgtm/config/tempo.yaml`). The inner `sum by (service, span_name)` drops it — but a query that skips that aggregation and only adds `target` would leave `source="tempo"` in place, and every edge would then claim to start at a node called `tempo`.

panels.title: Call matrix — chord
panels.description:
Route A once more, as a chord. Every pair keeps both directions as separate ribbons, which is what makes the `grafana ↔ prometheus` relationship legible: Grafana queries Prometheus for dashboards, Prometheus scrapes Grafana's `/metrics`, and those are two different flows with two different rates.

`Mean` over the window rather than `Last`, so a single quiet scrape interval does not empty an arc. The self-loop (`prometheus → prometheus`) draws as a ribbon that returns to its own arc.

panels.title: Route B before Rows to fields — why organize is not optional
panels.description:
The raw instant response the two Route B panels start from, with an empty Transform tab so the columns are visible.

Read them left to right: `client`, `dst`, `edge`, `server`, `src`, `Value` — **alphabetical**, because Prometheus sorts label columns by name and `Time` leads. `rowsToFields` takes the *first string column* as the mark name, so with no `organize` every mark would be named after its client: five fields called `grafana`, `prometheus` or `user`, several of them duplicates, none of them carrying `source` / `target` labels, and no graph at all.

`organize` fixes three things in one step — it drops `Time` and the leftover `client` / `server` columns that would otherwise become stray labels, moves `edge` to position 0, and renames `src` / `dst` to the contract's `source` / `target`. `filterFieldsByName` cannot reorder and `renameByRegex` only sets `config.displayName`, leaving `field.name` untouched, so neither is a substitute.
